classification.difficultyReason: Combine equal tangent lengths from three external points with ordered-segment sums to establish equality of indirect tangent and intersection lengths.

content.prompt:
Take two non-intersecting circles in the plane with centres $O$ and $O'$. Draw two indirect common tangents $AA'$ and $BB'$, and one direct tangent $CC'$, where $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on the first circle, and $A'$, $B'$ and $C'$ lie on the second circle.

Produce $AA'$ and $BB'$ to meet $CC'$ at $X$ and $Y$.

spec.description: Two disjoint circles with two crossing indirect tangents and one direct tangent.
spec.mathematics: Tangent normals solve signed-distance equations for centres(-2,0),(2,0),radii.7,1. All six contact points and X/Y/M intersections are exact. Dense labelled tangent network needs the explicitly larger width; final height and labels remain unreviewed.
spec.answerVisibility: Original givens and necessary labels only; no calculated answers.

sizing.exceptionReason: Proof construction, source relationships and full10pt labels determine size; final width and height require source-side rendered review.

answer.worked:
Let $M$ be the intersection of the indirect tangents. Tangents from the same external point have equal lengths, so $MA=MB$ and $MA'=MB'$. Since $M$ lies between the circles,
$$AA'=AM+MA'=BM+MB'=BB'.$$

Equal tangent lengths from $X$ give $XC=XA$ and $XC'=XA'$. From $Y$, $YC=YB$ and $YC'=YB'$.

Using the order shown on the direct and indirect tangents,
$$\begin{align*}XY&=XA+AA'-YC',\\XY&=YB'+BB'-XC.\end{align*}$$
Adding and substituting the equal tangent lengths gives
$$2XY=AA'+BB'=2AA'.$$
Therefore $XY=AA'$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Describe what happens when the two circles are touching each other externally.

answer.short: The two indirect tangents merge into the common tangent at the contact point; $AA'=BB'=XY=0$.
answer.worked: At external contact the paired contact points of both indirect tangents coincide at the touching point. The two indirect tangents become the same common tangent there, so $A=A'=B=B'$ and $X=Y$. Consequently all three lengths are zero.
